body:
@sepo-agent /answer 

how to support installing them properly and configure it properly ?

comments.body:
Short answer: Sepo does **not** currently have first-class MCP setup. The right implementation is to add MCP as a runtime configuration layer, not as prompt text.

Current relevant architecture:

- Runtime setup only installs Node, Sepo deps, and optionally Codex/Claude CLIs: [`.github/actions/setup-agent-runtime/action.yml`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.github/actions/setup-agent-runtime/action.yml#L1-L28), [install steps](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.github/actions/setup-agent-runtime/action.yml#L104-L140).
- Agent execution passes fixed GitHub/provider credentials into `.agent/dist/run.js`: [`.github/actions/run-agent-task/action.yml`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.github/actions/run-agent-task/action.yml#L442-L456).
- Runtime env mapping only covers GitHub, OpenAI, Claude, and Anthropic credentials today: [`.agent/src/runtime-env.ts`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/src/runtime-env.ts#L29-L61).
- ACPX invocation/session setup only configures model, reasoning, and permission mode: [`.agent/src/acpx-adapter.ts`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/src/acpx-adapter.ts#L345-L458), [run path](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/src/acpx-adapter.ts#L789-L915).
- The public configuration list has no MCP variable/secret yet: [`.agent/docs/customization/configuration-list.md`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/docs/customization/configuration-list.md#L5-L41).

Recommended approach:

1. Add `AGENT_MCP_POLICY` as a repository variable for non-secret config: enabled routes, provider targets, server definitions, and allowed commands.
2. Add one explicit repository secret, `AGENT_MCP_ENV`, as JSON for MCP credentials. Do not try to reference arbitrary GitHub secret names from JSON; Actions cannot safely/dynamically expose them.
3. Add a typed `.agent/src/mcp-config.ts` plus CLI, for example `.agent/src/cli/setup-mcp.ts`, that validates policy, merges secret env, and writes provider-specific MCP configuration.
4. Wire `setup-agent-runtime` / `run-agent-task` so MCP setup happens after Codex/Claude CLI installation and before `.agent/dist/run.js`.
5. Configure providers using their CLIs where possible:
   - Codex has `codex mcp add` for stdio and HTTP MCP servers.
   - Claude has `claude mcp add` / `claude mcp add-json`.
6. Keep default `AGENT_MCP_POLICY` disabled. Enable per route/server, for example `answer` can use read-only docs/search servers, while `implement` can opt into stronger tools only when explicitly configured.
7. Document this in `configuration-list.md`, `setup-guide.md`, and self-hosted runner docs, including version pinning and security notes.

Example target config shape:

```json
{
  "enabled": true,
  "route_overrides": {
    "answer": ["docs"],
    "implement": ["docs", "repo-tools"]
  },
  "servers": {
    "docs": {
      "transport": "stdio",
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@example/mcp-docs-server@1.2.3"],
      "env": {
        "DOCS_API_KEY": { "from_secret_json": "DOCS_API_KEY" }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Execution plan before coding:

1. Confirm which providers must be supported first: Codex only, Claude only, or both.
2. Confirm whether MCP servers should be configured globally for all routes or only per-route.
3. Implement the typed policy parser and tests.
4. Add the MCP setup CLI and workflow/action inputs.
5. Add docs and one smoke-testable example.
6. Run `.agent` CI checks.

Please approve this direction before implementation.
